branch.name: Cloud & Ops
branch.summary: Operating running infrastructure: Kubernetes workloads, Docker containers, AWS resources (EC2, S3, Lambda, CloudWatch), observability (Grafana/Prometheus/Loki, Datadog logs, metrics, monitors, traces) and incident paging/on-call (PagerDuty). Use for debugging prod, scaling, rollbacks, log and metric queries, alerts and paging people.

toolkits.name: Kubernetes
toolkits.summary: kubectl-style operations (get, describe, logs, scale, rollout, apply, exec) against the clusters in the local kubeconfig.

tools.name: kubectl_get
tools.description: Get or list Kubernetes resources by resource type, name, and optionally namespace

resourceType.description: Type of resource to get (e.g., pods, deployments, services, configmaps, events, nodes, etc.)

name.description: Name of the resource (optional - if not provided, lists all resources of the specified type)

allNamespaces.description: If true, list resources across all namespaces

sortBy.description: Sort events by a field (default: lastTimestamp). Only applicable for events.

tools.name: kubectl_describe
tools.description: Describe Kubernetes resources by resource type, name, and optionally namespace

resourceType.description: Type of resource to describe (e.g., pods, deployments, services, etc.)

name.description: Name of the resource to describe

allNamespaces.description: If true, describe resources across all namespaces

tools.name: kubectl_logs
tools.description: Get logs from Kubernetes resources like pods, deployments, or jobs. For deployments and jobs, logs are collected from the pods they manage. Use 'previous' to see output from the last terminated container instance (useful for CrashLoopBackOff), and 'since' or 'tail' to limit how much is returned.

resourceType.description: Type of resource to get logs from

container.description: Container name (required when pod has multiple containers)

tail.description: Number of lines to show from end of logs

previous.description: Include logs from previously terminated containers

follow.description: Follow logs output (not recommended, may cause timeouts)

tools.name: kubectl_scale
tools.description: Scale a Kubernetes deployment

name.description: Name of the deployment to scale

replicas.description: Number of replicas to scale to

resourceType.description: Resource type to scale (deployment, replicaset, statefulset)

tools.name: kubectl_rollout
tools.description: Manage the rollout of a resource (e.g., deployment, daemonset, statefulset)

resourceType.description: Type of resource to manage rollout for

revision.description: Revision to rollback to (for undo subcommand)

toRevision.description: Revision to roll back to (for history subcommand)

timeout.description: The length of time to wait before giving up (e.g., '30s', '1m', '2m30s')

watch.description: Watch the rollout status in real-time until completion

tools.name: kubectl_apply
tools.description: Apply a Kubernetes YAML manifest from a string or file

filename.description: Path to a YAML file to apply (optional - use either manifest or filename)

dryRun.description: If true, only validate the resource, don't apply it

force.description: If true, immediately remove resources from API and bypass graceful deletion

tools.name: kubectl_delete
tools.description: Delete Kubernetes resources by resource type, name, labels, or from a manifest file

resourceType.description: Type of resource to delete (e.g., pods, deployments, services, etc.)

name.description: Name of the resource to delete

labelSelector.description: Delete resources matching this label selector (e.g. 'app=nginx')

manifest.description: YAML manifest defining resources to delete (optional)

filename.description: Path to a YAML file to delete resources from (optional)

allNamespaces.description: If true, delete resources across all namespaces

force.description: If true, immediately remove resources from API and bypass graceful deletion

gracePeriodSeconds.description: Period of time in seconds given to the resource to terminate gracefully

tools.name: exec_in_pod
tools.description: Execute a command in a Kubernetes pod or container and return the output

name.description: Name of the pod to execute the command in

command.description: Command to execute in the pod (string or array of args)

container.description: Container name (required when pod has multiple containers)

shell.description: Shell to use for command execution (e.g. '/bin/sh', '/bin/bash'). If not provided, will use command as-is.

timeout.description: Timeout for command - 60000 milliseconds if not specified

tools.name: kubectl_context
tools.description: Manage Kubernetes contexts

name.description: Name of the context to set as current (required for set operation)

showCurrent.description: When listing contexts, highlight which one is currently active

detailed.description: Include detailed information about the context

toolkits.name: Docker
toolkits.summary: Manage containers and images on the local Docker engine.

tools.name: list_containers
tools.description: List all Docker containers

all.description: Show all containers (default shows just running)

filters.description: Filter containers by label, status or name

label.description: Filter by label, either `key` or `key=value` format

tools.name: run_container
tools.description: Create and start a Docker container from an image. Pulls the image first if it is not present locally. Returns the container ID and name. Prefer this over separate create/start calls; port mappings are given as {container_port: host_port}, e.g. {"5432/tcp": 5433}.

command.description: Command to run in the container

ports.description: A map whose keys are the container port, and the values are the host port(s) to bind to.

volumes.description: List of volume mounts in 'host_path:container_path[:ro]' format, or named volumes

network_mode.description: Network mode (bridge, host, none, or a named network)

auto_remove.description: Remove the container when it exits

MaximumRetryCount.description: Max restarts when Name is on-failure

tools.name: stop_container
tools.description: Stop a container

tools.name: fetch_container_logs
tools.description: Fetch logs for a Docker container

tail.description: Number of lines to show from the end of the logs, or 'all'

since.description: Only return logs since this time (unix timestamp or relative like '10m')

tools.name: pull_image
tools.description: Pull an image from a registry

tools.name: build_image
tools.description: Build a Docker image from a Dockerfile

path.description: Path to the build context directory

dockerfile.description: Path to Dockerfile relative to the context

no_cache.description: Do not use cache when building the image

target.description: Name of the build stage to target in a multi-stage Dockerfile

toolkits.name: AWS
toolkits.summary: Calls AWS APIs for EC2, S3, Lambda and CloudWatch (metrics, Logs Insights, alarms) using the configured AWS profile.

tools.name: ec2_describe_instances
tools.description: Describes the specified EC2 instances or all instances in a region. Supports filtering by tag, state, instance type, VPC and more using the standard EC2 filter syntax.

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to the profile's configured region.

next_token.description: Pagination token from a previous call

tools.name: ec2_manage_instances
tools.description: Start, stop, reboot or terminate one or more EC2 instances.

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to the profile's configured region.

hibernate.description: Hibernate instead of stop (stop only, instance must support it)

force.description: Force stop without flushing file system caches

dry_run.description: Check permissions without performing the action

tools.name: s3_list_buckets
tools.description: List buckets.

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to the profile's configured region.

tools.name: s3_list_objects
tools.description: List objects in an S3 bucket, optionally under a key prefix.

prefix.description: Only return keys beginning with this prefix

continuation_token.description: Token from a previous truncated listing

tools.name: s3_get_object
tools.description: Retrieve an object from S3. Text content is returned inline; binary objects are returned base64-encoded or saved to download_path.

download_path.description: Optional local path to save the object to

tools.name: s3_put_object
tools.description: Upload an object to S3 from inline content or a local file.

file_path.description: Local file to upload instead of body

tools.name: lambda_list_functions
tools.description: Lists functions

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to the profile's configured region.

max_items.description: Maximum number of functions to return

tools.name: lambda_invoke
tools.description: Invokes a Lambda function. Use RequestResponse to wait for the result, or Event to invoke asynchronously.

function_name.description: Function name, ARN, or partial ARN

payload.description: JSON payload passed to the function

log_type.description: Set to Tail to include the last 4KB of execution log in the response

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to the profile's configured region.

tools.name: cloudwatch_get_metric_data
tools.description: Retrieve CloudWatch metric values for AWS resources (EC2, RDS, ELB, Lambda, SQS, etc.) over a time range. Specify the namespace, metric name and dimensions, plus the statistic and period to aggregate by.

end_time.description: End of the range (ISO 8601). Defaults to now.

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to the profile's configured region.

tools.name: cloudwatch_logs_insights_query
tools.description: Executes a CloudWatch Logs Insights query against one or more log groups and waits for the results. Use this to search and aggregate log events from Lambda functions, ECS tasks, API Gateway, VPC flow logs and anything else shipping to CloudWatch Logs. The query uses Logs Insights syntax, e.g. 'fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /ERROR/ | sort @timestamp desc | limit 50'. Time range defaults to the last hour. Large time ranges over busy log groups can be slow and costly; narrow the range where possible.

limit.description: Maximum number of log events to return

max_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the query to complete

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to the profile's configured region.

tools.name: cloudwatch_describe_alarms
tools.description: Gets CloudWatch alarms and their current state.

state_value.description: Only return alarms in this state

alarm_name_prefix.description: Only return alarms whose name starts with this prefix

region.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to the profile's configured region.

toolkits.name: Grafana
toolkits.summary: Grafana dashboards, alert rules, OnCall schedules, and queries against its Prometheus and Loki datasources.

tools.name: search_dashboards
tools.description: Search for dashboards

tools.name: get_dashboard_by_uid
tools.description: Retrieves the complete dashboard, including panels, variables, and settings, for a specific dashboard identified by its UID.

tools.name: query_prometheus
tools.description: Query Prometheus using a PromQL expression. Supports both instant queries (at a single point in time) and range queries (over a time range). Time can be specified either in RFC3339 format or as relative time expressions like 'now', 'now-1h', 'now-30m', etc.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

startTime.description: The start time. Required if queryType is 'range', ignored if queryType is 'instant'. Supported formats are RFC3339 or relative to now (e.g. 'now', 'now-1.5h', 'now-2h45m').

endTime.description: The end time. Required if queryType is 'range', ignored if queryType is 'instant'.

stepSeconds.description: The time series step size in seconds. Required if queryType is 'range'.

queryType.description: The type of query to use. Either 'range' or 'instant'

tools.name: query_loki_logs
tools.description: Executes a LogQL query against a Loki datasource to retrieve log entries or metric values. Returns a list of results, each containing a timestamp, labels, and either a log line or a metric value. Defaults to the last hour and a limit of 10 entries. Prefer using list_loki_label_names first to discover the labels available.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

logql.description: The LogQL query to execute against Loki. This can be a simple label matcher or a complex query with filters, parsers, and expressions

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format

limit.description: Optionally, the maximum number of log lines to return (max: 100)

direction.description: Optionally, the direction of the query

tools.name: list_alert_rules
tools.description: Lists Grafana alert rules, returning a summary including UID, title, current state (e.g., 'pending', 'firing', 'inactive'), and labels. Supports filtering by labels using selectors and pagination.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return

name.description: The name of the label to match against

label_selectors.description: Optionally, a list of matchers to filter alert rules by labels

tools.name: get_current_oncall_users
tools.description: Get users currently on-call for a specific Grafana OnCall schedule ID. Returns the schedule ID, name, and a list of detailed user objects for those currently on call.

scheduleId.description: The ID of the schedule to get current on-call users for

toolkits.name: Datadog
toolkits.summary: Datadog logs, metrics, monitors, APM traces, dashboards and incidents.

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description: Search and retrieve logs from Datadog

query.description: Datadog log search query, e.g. 'service:checkout status:error'

limit.description: Maximum number of logs to return

tools.name: query_metrics
tools.description: Query timeseries points of metrics from Datadog

from.description: Start of the queried time period in epoch seconds

to.description: End of the queried time period in epoch seconds

tools.name: get_monitors
tools.description: Fetch the status of Datadog monitors

groupStates.description: States to filter (e.g., alert, warn, no data, ok)

tools.name: list_traces
tools.description: Retrieve a list of APM traces (spans) from Datadog, filtered by query, service, operation and time range. Useful for finding slow or failing requests.

tools.name: list_dashboards
tools.description: Get a list of dashboards from Datadog

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: Get incidents

toolkits.name: PagerDuty
toolkits.summary: PagerDuty incidents (list, create/trigger, acknowledge, resolve, notes) and on-call schedules.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: List incidents. By default returns incidents assigned to the current user; set request_scope to 'all' to see every incident in the account.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: Get an incident.

tools.name: create_incident
tools.description: Create an incident in PagerDuty. This triggers notifications to the on-call responders of the given service according to its escalation policy.

title.description: A succinct description of the problem

assignments.description: Assign directly to users instead of the escalation policy

tools.name: manage_incidents
tools.description: Manage one or more incidents: acknowledge, resolve, change urgency, reassign or escalate.

escalation_level.description: Escalate to this level of the escalation policy

tools.name: add_note_to_incident
tools.description: Add a note to an incident timeline.

tools.name: list_oncalls
tools.description: List the on-call entries (who is on call, for which schedule and escalation policy, and until when).

earliest.description: Only return the earliest on-call for each combination of escalation policy, level and user
